audit.why: Rare among this champion's entries: the content layer's win[] and the full layer's phases[].side agree with each other AND with the packet levelChart at all seven stages — Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Sion — and the whys[] narrative matches stage for stage. At 52.44% over 757 games that shape is right: even at 1, Ambessa's from 2 through first item, Sion's once he has HP and armour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Unstoppable Onslaught is never named or described in either layer. The only references are phases[4].why's generic "Sion's ultimate changes the math too" and late's "teamfight knockup", which the same paragraph attributes to Decimating Smash.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Sion charges in a direction, ramping up speed over time. He can steer his charge slightly with the mouse cursor location. When he collides with an enemy he deals damage and knocks them up based on the distance he has charged." Three things matter and none are stated. It is 140s at rank 1, so it is a real cooldown to track. It is steerable, so it is not dodged by walking sideways the way a straight-line charge is. And the knockup scales with distance charged, which means the correct answer is to meet him early rather than let him accelerate — the opposite of the instinct to back away.
audit.corrected: Named with its cooldown, steering and distance-scaled knockup in spikes[3], late, wants.foe[2], phases[4].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Furnace is mentioned five times and only ever as a shield to avoid trading into. Its reactivation is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Sion shields himself and can reactivate after 3 seconds to deal Magic Damage to enemies nearby." It is a delayed point-blank damage instance, not just mitigation, so the advice "don't force extended fights into a fresh Soul Furnace shield" is right for the wrong reason and leaves out the part that actually punishes you — standing next to him three seconds after he shields. It is 15s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: The 3-second detonation written into spikes[1], mid, whys[3], breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[1] and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Roar of the Slayer is named four times as "armor-shred poke" but its minion behaviour is never stated, and the entry twice implies that standing behind the wave is safe.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Sion fires a short range shockwave that damages and slows and reduces the Armor of the first enemy hit. If the shockwave hits a minion or monster, it will be knocked back, damaging, slowing, and reducing the Armor of all enemies that it passes through." So a minion between you and Sion does not absorb it — the minion becomes the projectile and carries the full damage, slow and armour shred into you. At 800 range that is most of the lane. For a champion who is told repeatedly to farm at the edge of her cone, this is the single most relevant thing about his poke.
audit.corrected: Written into early, wants.foe[1], dontsFull[2] and breakdown.cooldowns with the real 12s cooldown and 800 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] recommends buying anti-heal early because "his healing fights your pattern". Sion has no healing in lane.
audit.why: The only healing anywhere in Sion's kit is Glory in Death: "After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate with rapidly decaying Health. His attacks become very rapid, heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health." That is post-mortem only. Buying Grievous Wounds early against a champion who cannot heal until he has already died is a wasted component for the entire laning phase; the item is worth a slot later, for the zombie state and for whatever the rest of their team brings. _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup for needs-antiheal and it is technically true, but the timing it implies is wrong.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal moved from an early buy to a late one, with the zombie state named as the only thing it answers; the zombie state's max-health scaling added to late and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] says "Hold W (Repudiation) to brace his E armor-shred poke or his Q slam so the blocked champion damage amplifies your next hit".
audit.why: Riot's Repudiation text: "If she blocked any non-minion damage while bracing herself, this ability will deal increased damage." The bonus goes to Repudiation's own slam, not to the next ability. A reader who braces and then saves the slam for later throws the entire bonus away — which is the exact mistake the wording invites.
audit.corrected: Restated so the bonus lands on Repudiation's slam, and pointed at the two damage instances worth bracing: the Q slam and the Soul Furnace detonation.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade" error, and the entry carries no cooldown numbers despite eight sequencing cues that all say "when his Q is down".
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants no shield. And "when his Q is down" needs a duration to be usable: Decimating Smash is 10s at rank 1 falling to 6s, so the window shrinks fast, while Soul Furnace is 15s, Roar of the Slayer 12s and Unstoppable Onslaught 140s. Those four numbers turn eight vague cues into eight timed ones.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why corrected and the numbers written into spikes[3], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1], dontsFull[2], phases[4].why and report[5].

edits.before: Public Execution blinks you behind him and suppresses him out of the fight, and the suppress lands through his Soul Furnace shield, so if his Decimating Smash is on cooldown a farm lane becomes a kill.
edits.after: Public Execution blinks to him and suppresses him out of the fight — and Soul Furnace is not just a shield, it re-detonates after 3 seconds for magic damage, so time the crash to land after it pops.

edits.before: Sion's window: a fully-charged Decimating Smash knockup interrupts your Drakehound's Step dash chain, stacked armor blunts your all-physical burst, and his zombie passive lets him keep swinging after you 'kill' him in a teamfight.
edits.after: Sion's window: Unstoppable Onslaught is 140s at rank 1 and its knockup scales with how far he has charged, a fully-charged Decimating Smash interrupts your dash chain, and the zombie passive keeps him swinging after you kill him.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash: Sion just wants to shove and chip you with his E (Roar of the Slayer) armor-shred poke, and you only have one ability, so last-hit and don't throw a naked Q he can step back from. The lane turns at 2 and 3: once your Q cone unlocks the Sundering Slam follow-up and your passive dash lets you weave an empowered auto, you out-trade his one-point Decimating Smash and his cooldown-bound E easily. The one thing to respect is a fully-charged Decimating Smash. If you see him stand still and charge it, the knockup will interrupt your dash, so bait it out or sidestep before you commit your Q.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash: Sion shoves and chips you with Roar of the Slayer, which shreds armour and reaches 800 — and if it clips a minion the minion is knocked back through you carrying the same damage, slow and shred, so hiding behind the wave does not help. You only have one ability, so last-hit and don't throw a naked Q. The lane turns at 2 and 3: your Q cone unlocks the Sundering Slam follow-up and the passive dash weaves an empowered auto, out-trading his one-point Decimating Smash. The one thing to respect is a fully-charged Q — the knockup interrupts your dash, so bait it or sidestep.

edits.before: This is your best stretch, but keep it honest. Through 4-5 trade only when his Decimating Smash is down and bank small leads rather than forcing extended fights into a fresh Soul Furnace shield. At 6 your Public Execution blinks you behind him and the suppress lands through that shield, and if his Q is on cooldown that's a real kill, not just a chunk. Don't dump R into him while his Soul Furnace is fresh and his Q is up, though, because that's how an even lane hands Sion a free zombie-state revenge kill on the way down.
edits.after: This is your best stretch, but keep it honest. Through 4-5 trade only when Decimating Smash is down, and remember Soul Furnace reactivates after 3 seconds to damage everything near him — leaving before the second half is the trade. At 6 Public Execution blinks to him and suppresses, and if his Q is on cooldown that's a real kill, not just a chunk. Don't dump R into a fresh Soul Furnace with his Q up, though, because that's how an even lane hands Sion a free zombie-state revenge kill on the way down.

edits.before: Honest truth: late game tilts to Sion, not you. Your damage is entirely physical, so once he stacks max HP and armor and his zombie passive lets him keep swinging after you 'kill' him, your burst stops closing fights. A fully-charged Decimating Smash also becomes a fight-ender, knocking up your whole side and canceling the dash chain your kit relies on. Win the lane on your level 6 and Eclipse windows, take plates and tower, and convert that lead into objectives before his scaling and teamfight knockup make this a problem you can't solo.
edits.after: Honest truth: late game tilts to Sion. Your damage is entirely physical, so once he stacks max HP and armour and the zombie state keeps him swinging after you kill him, your burst stops closing fights — and those zombie attacks heal him off your maximum health, which is the only place Grievous Wounds is worth a slot. Unstoppable Onslaught knocks up harder the further he has charged, so meet him early rather than letting him build speed. Win the lane on your level 6 and Eclipse windows and convert to objectives.

notes:
This was the cleanest entry in the slice — zero packet defects, eight sequencing cues, and a level chart that already agreed with itself, with the packet, and with its own whys[] at all seven stages. I marked point 2 correct rather than inventing a disagreement. The work here was additive: three abilities were under-described (Unstoppable Onslaught not mentioned at all, Soul Furnace's 3-second detonation missing, Roar of the Slayer's minion bounce missing) and one item recommendation had the timing backwards.

The minion-bounce on Roar of the Slayer is the most useful addition for a melee champion who is told all through the entry to farm at the edge of her cone. A minion in the way does not block it; the minion becomes the delivery vehicle and everything it passes through takes the damage, slow and armour shred.

ANTI-HEAL TIMING: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for this pair via Glory in Death, and report[8] duly recommended Oblivion Orb early. Glory in Death only exists after Sion has been killed, so an early Grievous Wounds component does nothing for the whole laning phase. I moved it late rather than removing it, since the zombie state's healing is real.

No "R passive armor-pen" or "Medarda Maxim" fabrications in this matchup, unlike most of the slice — but both are still outstanding elsewhere in champ-data/content/ambessa.js and champ-data/ambessa.full.js and are worth a global grep.

KIT-FILE DATA WARNING: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json carries spurious "heal" and "grounding" flags on Public Execution and a spurious "grounding" flag on Repudiation. Sion's Decimating Smash is also flagged "slow", which is not in Riot's description of it.
